caveats.title: “Safe” is a proxy label
caveats.text: “Safe” is a derived proxy label: mean slope <8° and hazard fraction <0.05. It is not an observed landing outcome or validated safety assessment.

caveats.title: Mixed results
caveats.text: Numerically, the QCNN reduces the reported regression errors and false-positive rate, but the CNN has higher safe recall and coverage. These results therefore do not identify a clear overall winner.

caveats.title: Pipeline comparison, not equal capacity
caveats.text: Thus the real-data experiment compares a full end-to-end CNN with a small head on a supervised frozen representation; it is a pipeline comparison, not an architecture-only or equal-capacity comparison.

caveats.title: No matched classical head
caveats.text: QCNN consumes a frozen supervised CNN representation and has far fewer trainable parameters. No real-data matched classical-head control is present in this primary Mars comparison, so numerical differences cannot be attributed specifically to quantum computation.

caveats.title: Five sites are the replication units
caveats.text: Five sites are the geographic replication units. Tiles within a site are not independent site-level observations. Three random seeds do not create more independent sites.

caveats.title: Terrain-proxy results
caveats.text: These are terrain-proxy results, not evidence for operational landing safety.

caveats.title: No quantum advantage claimed
caveats.text: All quantum circuits were simulated numerically on classical hardware. No quantum advantage or superiority is claimed.

caveats.title: Corrected Moon CNN parameter count
caveats.text: The independent audit correctly establishes 59,347 trainable parameters during CNN fitting, with the 195-parameter classifier remaining trainable after encoder freeze.

caveats.title: Timings are not comparable
caveats.text: CNN timing includes image-encoder inference, while recorded QCNN timing is for the head on already-computed embeddings. It excludes the encoder and is not an apples-to-apples end-to-end latency comparison.

caveats.title: Class imbalance
caveats.text: The majority baseline’s 68.42% test accuracy is correct but predicts no minority classes (balanced accuracy 0.333, macro-F1 0.271). Accuracy alone is therefore misleading.

caveats.title: Different training regimes
caveats.text: This can support a frozen-embedding head comparison, not a clean end-to-end CNN-versus-QCNN attribution.

caveats.title: Descriptive evidence only
caveats.text: Three seeds on one supplied split are descriptive evidence, not proof of a general advantage.

caveats.title: Seeds are not independent test samples
caveats.text: The three-seed mean ± SD is not a confidence interval. The same fixed test partition is reused across seeds, so seeds reflect initialization/training variation, not independent test samples.

caveats.title: Unverified provenance
caveats.text: The provenance audit did not verify class annotation criteria, original split-generation methodology, source-image identity, or geographic/site identity.

caveats.title: Test-embedding timing in the completed run
caveats.text: Test embeddings were computed before fitting the QCNN/MLP heads, but were not used for gradient updates, validation selection, or threshold selection; the saved audit confirms final metrics came from saved predictions.
